summary: Phase H full backend + frontend test. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_phase_h.py (27 tests, xdist-safe, RUN_PREFIX TEST_userH_) covering push endpoints, notify() push fanout (mocked push.webpush), 410 pruning, discussions (blog/forum + approval + cascade delete), digest send_history and _sunday_digest_job. Full regression: 315 passed / 13 skipped / 2 xfailed / 0 failed across all Phase A-H suites. VAPID key persistence verified across a backend restart (same 87-char key, no second 'generated fresh VAPID keypair' log line, exactly 1 db.settings doc). UI verified with Playwright: Community Hub (forum instant publish, blog pending hidden from non-admin, admin pending-drafts + Approve -> published), /digest recap card ('Recent sends' with dates) + browser-push subscribe/unsubscribe with mocked serviceWorker/Notification (GET /push/vapid-public-key + POST /push/subscribe + POST /push/unsubscribe all fired, push-off-btn/push-on-btn toggled), /admin/events filters (search/market/source + count line) and mobile 390px layout (no horizontal overflow). ONE CRITICAL functional bug found: the persisted VAPID private key is a PKCS8 PEM, which py_vapid/pywebpush cannot parse, so every REAL push delivery fails (sent always 0). Mocked tests hid this.

critical.issue: VAPID private key is stored/passed as a PKCS8 PEM ('private_pem'). pywebpush calls py_vapid.Vapid.from_string(), which strips newlines and b64url-decodes -> ValueError: 'Could not deserialize key data ... ASN.1 parsing error: invalid length'. Reproduced on the preview backend: POST /api/push/test with a real-format FCM endpoint returns {"sent":0} and logs '[push] unexpected error' with that traceback. Result: NO web push notification can ever be delivered in production. Verified fix direction (probe run locally): py_vapid accepts base64url raw 32-byte private value OR base64url DER, e.g. b64url(pk.private_numbers().private_value.to_bytes(32,'big')) — store that (or write the PEM to a file and pass the file path). New regression test TestVapidKeyFormat::test_stored_private_key_is_loadable_by_py_vapid currently FAILS and will pass once fixed; existing persisted db.settings {key:'vapid'} doc must be migrated/regenerated.

minor.issue: Non-WebPushException failures fall into the generic `except Exception` branch, so a permanently-broken key looks like a transient error and is only visible in logs; consider surfacing a health signal or failing loudly once at startup (e.g. validate the key with Vapid.from_string when generating/loading).
Body {} returns 422 (Pydantic) while {subscription:{keys:{}}} returns 400 — inconsistent but acceptable; documented in tests.

critical_code_review_comments: push.py: never pass a PEM to pywebpush's vapid_private_key; it expects a b64url raw/DER string or a file path. Validate the key once at generation time (Vapid.from_string) so a bad format fails fast instead of silently swallowing every send.

push.py: pruning only triggers on WebPushException with response.status_code in (404,410); real pywebpush errors that surface as plain ValueError/requests errors go to the catch-all and are indistinguishable from transient failures.
notifications.notify(): the push fanout is awaited inline, so a slow/hanging push service will slow every notification-producing request — consider asyncio.create_task or a timeout.
hub_router.list_discussions: sorts on published_at, which is null for pending docs — ordering of the admin pending list is effectively undefined; sort on created_at for non-published statuses.

rca_of_the_issue: push._ensure_vapid_keys() serializes the generated EC key with serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8/Encoding.PEM and stores it as 'private_pem'; send_push_to_user passes that string as vapid_private_key. pywebpush >= 1.x forwards it to py_vapid.Vapid.from_string(), which does private_key.encode().replace(b'\n', b'') then b64urldecode() — a PEM's '-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----' header makes the decode produce garbage, raising ValueError('Could not deserialize key data ... ASN.1 parsing error: invalid length'). send_push_to_user catches it in its generic except, logs '[push] unexpected error' and returns 0, so the API still answers 200 {"sent":0} and no notification is ever delivered. Reproduction: insert a push_subscriptions doc with a real-format FCM endpoint for a user, POST /api/push/test with that user's token, then check backend.err.log. Probe (/tmp/vapid_probe.py) confirms py_vapid accepts b64url(raw 32-byte private value) and b64url(DER) but not PEM.
